hints.title: Perimeter Divisibility and Target Side
hints.text: A square requires four identical side lengths. If the total perimeter cannot be divided evenly into four parts, forming a square is impossible.

hints.title: Descending Pruning Invariant
hints.text: Sorting sticks from longest to shortest places larger constraints first, triggering immediate cutoffs when a large stick overflows any remaining side allowance.

hints.title: Four Bucket Assignment Procedure
hints.text: Maintain an array of four bucket sums. For each matchstick, attempt placement in any bucket where the sum remains under the target side length. If a bucket remains empty after trying a stick, terminate exploration across remaining symmetric empty buckets immediately.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: input size or search state bound
complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(4^(N/4)) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Without descending sorting or zero-pruning, exploring 4^n assignments on 15 sticks exceeds execution limits.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Pruned backtracking or bitmask memoization checks valid 4-partitions in O(4^(n/4)) time with O(n) call stack space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should check divisibility by 4, sort descending for early pruning, and break on empty side symmetrically.
